title: Progressive Importance-Guided Observation with Memory for Resource-Constrained Autonomous Robots
content: Efficient observation is essential for long-term autonomous robots because continuous and exhaustive sensing wastes computational resources while important or newly emerging information may still be missed. However, existing observation strategies often lack a unified mechanism for prioritizing impor-tant information, progressively covering initially neglected regions, adapting observation frequency to environmental change, and avoiding repeated processing of already understood information. This paper proposes Progressive Importance-Guided Observation (PIGO), which allocates limited detailed-observation capacity according to importance, uncertainty, novelty, and coverage demand. The method progressively shifts attention from urgent information toward neglected candidates, adapts observa-tion intervals according to environmental stability and change, and maintains viewpoint-conditioned observation memory to detect novelty, relation changes, removals, and true environmental changes. Stable low-impact information that has already been processed can be suppressed and reactivated when its state or relevance changes. Simulation and real-robot experiments show that PIGO achieves hidden-critical recall of 0.700 at a 35% observation budget, reduces repeated benign processing from 0.2964 to 0.0965, and decreases viewpoint false-change rate from 1.000 to 0.000.
